summary: Introductory onboarding and sprint planning for Cedar Dataworks' Redwood deployment. Reviewed roles, timeline, env options (hosted/dedicated/private), and security controls. Agreed to provision sandbox and share compliance artifacts; planned technical deep dive next week.
topics: Deployment flavor tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
Sprint plan: milestones, owners, and checkpoints
Benchmarks and evals: perf targets and sample data
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-15
Start: 14:00 PT | Duration: ~56 min
Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, I'll be your AE/CSM and kinda shepherd the onboarding. Diego from SE is here to talk infra.
[00:12] Lena (Cedar): Hi all, Lena here. We're excited — want to get this rolled fast, need predictable latency for inference and safe data handling.
[00:25] Diego (Redwood): Quick intro from me. I've worked on a few private deployments and dedicated clusters, we can map to your VPC or do hosted to start.
[01:05] Tom (Cedar): For infra context, we run most stuff in a locked-down VPC, have strict egress rules, and an internal jumpbox flow. We'll need to know required ports and IP ranges.
[01:40] Maya: Great, that maps to the checklist. Sana, want to surface security asks?
[01:47] Sana (Cedar): Yeah. SOC 2 report, KMS integration for keys, SSO with SAML, RBAC and audit logs are must-haves. Also, data residency — some models may touch EU data.
[02:10] Diego: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM for Private builds, SAML/SSO is standard for Console. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM. We'll capture those in the security doc I send.
[02:35] Ethan (Cedar): Timeline — we're aiming to have an initial pilot in 6 weeks, with two-week sprints after that. Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for typical prompts, and cost per 1k tokens under our target.
[03:05] Maya: Sounds reasonable, we'll align sprint milestones today. Suggest sandbox in week 1, ingest sample data & run baseline in week 2, perf tuning in week 3.
[03:40] Lena: Sandbox access and a test harness would be ideal. We have internal prompts and a small labeled set.
[04:05] Diego: We'll provision a sandbox dedicated pool that mirrors production config but scaled down. Note: continuous batching settings and KV cache behavior will change cost/latency; we'll show recommended profiles.
[04:45] Tom: How heavy is the agent? We have some air-gapped segments.
[04:50] Diego: The agent is small; for fully air-gapped we can do an on-prem package, but if you can open an allowlist to the control plane that's fastest. We'll document both paths.
[05:20] Maya: Ok two paths: hosted quickstart vs private on-prem. Which do you prefer for pilot?
[05:30] Lena: Prefer private in our VPC so we can validate compliance earlier.
[05:35] Sana: Agree, better for audits.
[06:00] Diego: For private, we'll need VPC CIDR, outbound rules, and a bastion host plan. I'll note the port list: TLS outbound and a couple of service endpoints.
[06:35] Tom: We'll share CIDR and firewall owner.
[07:00] Maya: On the product side, we'll want to know your main workload: chat, generation, or embeddings?
[07:10] Ethan: Mostly chat + retrieval augmented generation. We'll also need embeddings for semantic search.
[07:30] Diego: Cool — retrieval means we'll look at embedding throughput and persistent caches. KV cache will help for chat vi session reuse.
[08:05] Lena: Are there sizing guidelines for document store + embeddings throughput?
[08:25] Diego: We'll give a baseline. Rough rule: X QPS of embedding calls maps to Y GPU throughput — I'll include a sizing spreadsheet.
[09:00] Maya: I'll send the onboarding playbook with the sizing template and prompt list.
[09:20] (transcription glitch) Speaker 2: ...and we also — uh — will provide the benchmahrk sheet.
[09:40] Diego: We should also capture performance SLA targets and acceptance criteria in the first sprint.
[10:00] Ethan: For acceptance we'll need reproducible evals against our sample prompts, and a cost report.
[10:25] Maya: Yep, Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and batching settings; we'll run A/B if needed.
[11:05] Sana: About keys — does Redwood store customer keys? We need KMS integration and never store raw keys in your cloud.
[11:20] Diego: We support customer KMS where keys are managed by you and used for encryption at rest; we do not persist plaintext keys. For some private setups you can bring an HSM.
[12:00] Tom: What about logs and PII redaction?
[12:10] Maya: You can configure redaction at ingestion and we have retention settings. We'll also provide audit log streaming.
[12:45] Lena: Great. Any blockers on legal side?
[12:50] Maya: We'll send standard SOW + SOC2 package; legal will ask, but for pilot we can start on a mutual NDA and a limited SOW.
[13:25] (crosstalk) Ethan: Can we try a short perf run on a 1k prompt set?
[13:35] Diego: Yes, once sandbox is up. We'll also share a small harness script.
[14:10] Maya: Ok let's run through a tentative sprint plan: Week 1 - sandbox provision + access; Week 2 - data ingestion + evals; Week 3 - tuning + security checklist; Week 4 - pilot wrap + decision.
[15:00] Lena: That schedule looks tight but doable.
[16:00] Diego: Tech notes — for dedicated hardware we recommend A100x or H100 depending on model family; quantized weights may change latency. We'll list model recommendations in the doc.
[16:45] Tom: If we need to switch to hosted for a burst, is that supported?
[16:50] Maya: Yes — Redwood supports smart routing and fallback to hosted capacity for bursts. We'll show routing policies and cost impact.
[17:20] Ethan: For cost, can we get an estimate baseline?
[17:30] Maya: We'll include a cost model; Diego will give per-token estimates for the recommended configs.
[18:00] (ambient noise)
[19:00] Diego: On telemetry — you'll get per-token latency, token counts, per-route cost in the console with traces.
[19:30] Lena: We'll need role-based access for the console; different teams need different views.
[19:40] Maya: We support RBAC and SSO mapping — we'll include AD/SAML mappings in the guide.
[20:05] Sana: Also need to confirm retention windows and e-discovery options.
[20:20] Maya: Noted. We'll detail retention config and log export routes.
[21:00] Ethan: Any third-party dependencies we should be aware of?
[21:10] Diego: Only standard cloud egress and optional object storage for model artifacts. For private, shipping a model artifact to your S3 or on-prem store is typical.
[22:05] Lena: Ok good. Are we planning an exec update cadence?
[22:15] Maya: Weekly check-ins during sprints and a bi-weekly exec summary.
[22:40] Tom: Who's the single point of contact?
[22:45] Maya: I'll be CSM lead; Diego is your SE contact for infra.
[23:10] (long pause)
[24:00] Maya: Any remaining questions?
[24:10] Sana: Nothing major — will follow up after we collate the compliance docs.
[24:30] Lena: We'll compile prompts and grab the dataset sample.
[25:00] Maya: Great. Quick recap — action items noted. We'll send the playbook and schedule the technical deep-dive for next Tues (proposed).
[25:25] Ethan: Works for us.
[25:40] Maya: Thanks everyone. End call.

Notes on quality: transcription had minor name mislabels and a short garbled line; audio intermittent for a minute around 18:00.
